course_subtitle: Learn how OCP volunteer leaders guide projects, community collaboration, contributions, and recognition programs.
course_description_html:
This course introduces the volunteer leadership roles that guide OCP projects, sub-projects, and workstreams. You’ll learn what each role is responsible for, the tools and processes leaders use to support community collaboration, and how contributions and recognition programs move through OCP.


Click START COURSE or select a lesson below.

blocks.body_html:
The Open Compute Project (OCP) brings at-scale innovations and hyperscaler best practices to all, spanning technology domains from the data center to the edge, and the technology stack from silicon, to systems, to site facilities and services.

The international OCP Community is made up of organizations and people from hyperscale and tier-2 cloud data center operators, communications providers, colocation providers, diverse enterprises, and technology vendors.

With the tenets of openness, impact, efficiency, scale and sustainability, the OCP engages and educates thousands of engineers every year. Across many projects and initiatives the OCP Foundation and Community are meeting the market today and shaping the future.

Click the play icon to watch the video.

Participating as a Volunteer Lead within the OCP Community allows you to share your expertise to help drive innovation. It is important to remember that your first priority in taking on this role should be to further the efforts of the international OCP Community.

blocks.body_html: As a Project or Sub-Project Lead within OCP, you play a crucial role in driving innovation, fostering collaboration, and ensuring the success of open hardware contributions.

This course is designed to help you understand your responsibilities, navigate the contribution process, and recognize the impact of your work within the OCP Community. By gaining a clear understanding of leadership expectations, contribution pathways, and recognition programs, you will be better equipped to lead effectively and support our mission of open and scalable computing solutions.

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

items_html: Explain the roles, responsibilities, and election processes of OCP Volunteer Leaders.
Describe the contribution types, submission processes, and guidelines within OCP.
Identify the OCP Accepted™, OCP Ready™, OCP S.A.F.E., and OCP Experience Center programs for products and data centers.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.body_html: At OCP, volunteer leaders take on specific roles that align with their expertise and commitment to advancing open hardware and software solutions.

These roles include:

  • Steering Committee Representative

  • Project Lead

  • Sub-Project Lead

  • Workstream Lead

Each position comes with distinct responsibilities and eligibility requirements.

Let's take a look at each one.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html: Steering Committee Representative

blocks.body_html: Steering Committee Representatives define the strategic direction of OCP projects. They identify industry challenges, drive the solution discovery process, and work closely with the OCP Board to ensure that project initiatives align with broader goals.

blocks.heading_html: Requirements

blocks.body_html: They must be employed by a Silver, Gold, or Platinum OCP Corporate Member organization. These positions are elected for a two-year term, while Steering Committee Chairs are appointed by the OCP Foundation.

items_html: Establishing yearly goals for the project community.
Providing feedback and guidance to incubated projects.
Creating and updating project charters.
Reviewing contributions for technical completeness.
Participating in Steering Committee meetings and voting on new contributions.

blocks.body_html: Project Leads are responsible for the successful delivery of project concepts and contributions. They ensure that all activities within the project align with the OCP Charter and the organization's mission.
They must be employed by a Startup, Bronze, Silver, Gold, or Platinum OCP Corporate Member organization. These positions are elected for a two-year term.

items_html: Establishing annual goals and leading the community in achieving them.
Facilitating discussions that promote open collaboration.
Communicating project objectives through OCP mailing lists, calls, and events.
Ensuring alignment between project activities and OCP’s overall direction.
Supporting the adoption of OCP solutions by sharing knowledge and best practices.
Updating the Wiki page to post call recordings, documents, and related contributions.

blocks.body_html: Sub-Project Leads manage specific components within larger OCP projects. They ensure technical contributions are in line with the project’s strategic direction and OCP’s overarching goals.
They must be employed by a Startup, Bronze, Silver, Gold, or Platinum OCP Corporate Member organization. These positions are elected for a two-year term.

items_html: Collaborating with Project Leads to achieve project goals.
Leading specialized discussions within the project.
Guiding new contributions in their area of expertise.
Encouraging participation from the OCP Community.
Updating the Wiki page to post call recordings, documents, and related contributions.

blocks.label: CONTINUE
blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.body_html: Workstream Leads oversee short-term initiatives such as hardware/software specifications, white papers, or best practice guidelines. Their goal is to ensure the successful completion of a well-defined work product.
They must be employed by an OCP Corporate Member organization. These positions are appointed for a finite duration based on project needs.

items_html: Coordinating a small group of companies to collaborate on a specific objective.
Understanding each company’s contribution to the workstream.
Maintaining regular meetings and documenting progress.
Working with OCP on legal and compliance matters.
Providing updates during project calls.
Presenting the final work product to the Steering Committee for review.
Updating the Wiki page to post call recordings, documents, and related contributions.

blocks.body_html:
Now that we've taken a look at the responsibilities and requirements for each role, let's explore the key steps in the election process for Project Leads, Sub-Project Leads, and Steering Committee Representatives.

Use the numbered controls to explore each stage.

items.title: Nominations
items.description_html:
Every election cycle begins with a Call for Nominations email sent to the OCP Community. Interested individuals can submit their nominations during this period.

Nomination period: 2 weeks

items.title: Voting
items.description_html:
Any member of the OCP Community who belongs to an OCP Corporate Member organization can vote for Project Leads and Sub-Project Leads.

Only members from Silver, Gold, or Platinum Corporate Member organizations can vote for Steering Committee Representatives, with each company receiving a set number of votes.

items.title: Timelines
items.description_html:
The election timeline differs depending on the role. Project Lead & Sub-Project Lead elections occur in even years, whereas Steering Committee Representative elections occur in odd years.

After nominations close, the community has two weeks to vote.

items.title: Results
items.description_html: Once the votes are counted, the election results are published via email to the entire OCP Community.

blocks.body_html: Once you have been elected as a Project Lead at OCP, you should get to know your Steering Committee Representative (who will act as your liaison to the Steering Committee) and your OCP Community Director.

The OCP Community Director will help you with any questions you might have about the OCP Community, including those about:

  • Your Project Community

  • Other Project Leaders and their Communities

  • OCP Foundation

  • OCP Policies and Operating Procedures

  • OCP Board
You should also get to know other members of the OCP Foundation Team as they can provide feedback based on their area of expertise related to your project.

blocks.heading_html: Getting to Know Your Project

blocks.body_html:
The success of each OCP Project depends on clear organization, up-to-date information, and effective collaboration. Getting to know your project is therefore essential, so let’s take a look at the key practices for managing an OCP Project, including coordinating meetings, maintaining the charter, and updating the project's wiki page.

Click each tab to learn more.

items.title: Coordinating Meetings
items.description_html:
Each project has a calendar located at the bottom of its Project Page, managed by OCP. To add participants or reschedule meetings, please speak with Michael Schill or Kevin Kifer.

Do not create separate meetings, as they will not appear on the official calendar.

Ensure that all meetings are recorded, except for those under CLA. While some CLA-related meetings may be recorded, they are not always published.

items.title: Maintaining the Charter
items.description_html:
Each project operates under a charter approved by the OCP Board of Directors, which is available on the OCP website under the respective project page. If updates are needed, collaborate with the Steering Committee Representative to make the necessary revisions.

Your project may include multiple sub-projects and workstreams. Take the time to familiarize yourself with them and their leadership. Ensure that the charter accurately reflects these components and remains up to date.

items.title: Updating the  Wiki page
items.description_html:
Each project has a dedicated Wiki Page (speak with Kevin Kifer for access). Here, you can collaborate with the existing Project Leads to ensure a smooth transition of responsibilities.

It's your responsibility to keep the Wiki updated with relevant content, as it serves as the primary source for work-in-progress information. Clearly label any unpublished or unofficial content as "DRAFT".

All call recordings are archived at the bottom of the page.

blocks.heading_html: Types of Projects

blocks.body_html:
The Open Compute Project consists of twelve key projects that focus on different aspects of open hardware innovation. These projects cover areas such as cooling, data center infrastructure, networking, security, storage, sustainability, and more.

Use the numbered controls to explore each project.

items.title: Networking
items.description_html: The Networking Project develops open, disaggregated network technologies to replace proprietary solutions, focusing on creating a fully open network stack.

items.title: Sustainability
items.description_html: The Sustainability Project supports data centers' net carbon-zero goals by promoting sustainable practices, introducing sustainability as the fifth OCP tenet, and offering open resources for industry-wide collaboration.

items.title: Security
items.description_html: The Security Project aims to enhance software security for IT hardware by providing standardized security implementations and frameworks, promoting industry-wide collaboration and open standards for improved cloud and IT security.

items.title: Storage
items.description_html: The Storage Project develops standards for storage components like chassis, sleds, and network-enabled storage, ensuring compatibility and scalability within the OCP ecosystem.

items.title: Time Appliances
items.description_html: The Time Appliances Project ensures accurate and reliable time synchronization across packet networks in industries like telecom and power, providing solutions to maintain optimal performance in distributed systems requiring precise time synchronization.

items.title: Open Platform Firmware
items.description_html: The Open Platform Firmware Project’s goal is to allow OCP owners to "own their firmware" by moving the point of control of firmware to the system owner.

items.title: Cooling Environments
items.description_html: The Cooling Environments Project develops efficient cooling solutions for high-performance computing, focusing on liquid cooling technologies like warm water cooling to manage heat in data centers.

items.title: AI Computing Continuum
items.description_html: The AI Computing Continuum Project advances open, modular infrastructure for AI across hyperscale-adjacent environments, helping the community build scalable, interoperable, and sustainable systems beyond traditional hyperscale data centers.

items.title: Rack & Power
items.description_html: The Rack & Power Project creates standardized rack solutions for data centers, integrating them with overall infrastructure to optimize energy efficiency and scalability.

items.title: Server
items.description_html: The Server Project focuses on creating standardized server specifications for scale computing, preventing fragmentation and enabling interoperable, high-performance servers that optimize deployment and adoption.

items.title: Data Center Facility
items.description_html: The Data Center Facility Project maximizes mechanical performance and thermal and electrical efficiency in data centers.

items.title: Hardware Management
items.description_html: The Hardware Management Project provides standardized tools for remotely managing machines in scale computing.

blocks.heading_html: Top Tips for Getting Started

blocks.body_html: To help you navigate your new role, here are some top tips to get started, stay organized, and effectively engage with the OCP Community.

items_html:
Stay on Top of Meetings
Know the meeting schedule, review upcoming agendas, and check past meeting minutes on the Wiki to understand the dynamics of a group and on-going discussions.

Understand the Contribution Pipeline
Track contributions at every stage, from proposal to voting, so you can effectively guide your project’s progress.

Learn about Contributions
Get familiar with the Contribution Spec Template and Contribution Portal – these are two key elements of the contribution process.

Seek Support
Connect with other Project Leads and Sub-Project Leads for guidance.

Engage with the Community
The OCP Community is an active resource – get involved with active discussions and seek advice when needed.

blocks.body_html:
As a Project Lead, setting clear goals ensures alignment with OCP’s mission and drives community engagement. By focusing on technology development, contributions, product growth, and infrastructure expansion, you can help shape the future of open hardware innovation. Below are five key areas to consider when defining your project’s goals.

Use the numbered controls to explore each goal.

items.title: Update the Charter
items.description_html: Work with the Steering Committee to review and update your project’s charter as needed. This ensures the project remains relevant, aligned with OCP principles, and effectively serves its intended purpose.

items.title: Align on Annual Goals
items.description_html: Collaborate with your Steering Committee Representative to define clear objectives for the year. These goals should reflect industry trends, community needs, and measurable outcomes that drive the project forward.

items.title: Define Technology Focus
items.description_html: Identify the key technologies your project should engage with or develop. This helps guide innovation efforts, ensures relevance within the broader OCP ecosystem, and attracts the right contributors.

items.title: Set Contribution Targets
items.description_html: Establish expectations for the number of contributions your project should receive over the year. Contributions may include technical specifications, design files, or implementation best practices.

items.title: Track Growth
items.description_html: Forecast how many OCP Accepted™ SKUs will emerge from your project, along with the number of integrated hardware/software solutions that leverage OCP technologies. If relevant, estimate the number of OCP Ready™ facilities that could be expected or impacted in the year ahead.

blocks.body_html: Contributions are essential for driving innovation in open-source hardware and data center technologies. OCP currently accepts twelve types of contributions, the most common being Specifications, Design Files, and Requirements Documents.

Contributions are circulated within the various OCP Project groups, and are protected and opened by a Contribution License Agreement.

Once finalized and approved by the project leadership, a contribution is brought to the Steering Committee for review and vote. If approved, the contribution is placed on the OCP website in the Contribution Database.

blocks.heading_html: Types of Specification

blocks.body_html:
To encourage multi-party collaboration that promotes more useful contributions, we've introduced a layered framework to produce three types of Specifications when making a contribution: Base Specification, Design Specification, and Product Specification.

Use the numbered controls to explore each specification.

items.title: Base Specification
items.description_html:
The Base Specification provides a high-level framework for interoperable hardware and software, driven by market needs.

To encourage broad participation, including from competitors, it contains minimal intellectual property content and requires a Contributor License Agreement.

Once the final Base Spec is submitted to OCP and approved by the Steering Committee, it will be published after a 30-day opt-out period has expired unless all participating companies select to waive the opt-out period.

items.title: Design Specification
items.description_html:
The Design Specification refines customer requirements based on the Base Spec, with participating companies developing detailed designs, including roadmaps and IP content.

This effort may involve a multi-party non-disclosure agreement. Once the final Design Spec is submitted to OCP and approved by the Steering Committee, it will be published after a 30-day opt-out period has expired unless all participating companies select to waive the opt-out period.

items.title: Product Specification
items.description_html:
The Product Specification defines manufacturing requirements based on the Design Specification, with fewer companies involved in creating a single spec.

The goal is to expand the number of products meeting the Design Specification. The final Product Spec is submitted to OCP and approved by the Steering Committee.

This will be published after a 30-day opt-out period has expired unless all participating companies select to waive the opt-out period.

blocks.heading_html: Managing the Contribution Process

items.description_html: Let's take a look at the key steps that need to be taken before presenting a contribution or proposal to the OCP Community, from ensuring the necessary agreements are in place to successfully navigating the submission, review, and approval process.

Contributor Requirements

Before presenting a proposal or contribution, ensure the contributor has the following in place:

  • The contributor must be a member of OCP and have signed a valid OCP Membership Agreement.

  • The contributor must sign a Contribution Licensing Agreement to clarify the licensing terms under which their contributions can be shared and used by the community.

Proposal Submission

The proposal or contribution should be presented via a document during a monthly call. You should work with the contributor to schedule a time slot, create an agenda, and inform OCP Community.

It should include details about the market need for the contribution, how it benefits the OCP Community, how it follows at least four OCP Tenets, a timeline, and any other relevant information.

Once these elements are in place, you'll need to upload the proposal to the Wiki as a Work in Progress (WIP).

Submission Requirements

If the proposal is accepted, the contributor(s) can start working on the contribution utilizing the correct OCP Template. When the Contribution is ready for review it should be submitted to the Contributor Portal. While in review, you will need to track its progress. If you are a Project Lead, you will need to accept the document for the contribution to move to the Steering Committee for review.

Steering Committee Review

Once accepted by the Project Lead and the Steering Committee Representative for the project, the contributor will be scheduled for a 10–15 minute presentation with the Steering Committee.

Feedback may be provided, so you will need to work with the contributor to ensure all requirements are met.

Voting and Approval

Once all requirements are met, the contribution is ready for a Vote. A majority vote is required for the approval by the Steering Committee. The Steering Committee will not begin reviewing or voting until all the previous steps are complete.

Upon approval, the contribution will be published in the OCP Contributions Database.

Summary

By following these steps, you can ensure a smooth process for presenting and approving contributions. Proper documentation, clear communication, and alignment with OCP’s core values are essential for successful contributions to the community.

Remember to track the process closely through the Contribution Portal and stay engaged with the Steering Committee for timely feedback and approval.

blocks.heading_html: Specification and Design File

blocks.body_html: Let's take a look at the steps for submitting a Specification or Design Package contribution.

items_html: Start in the Contribution Portal.

All Specification/Design Package contributions begin with a legal document that defines their scope – the Contribution License Agreement (CLA). OCP accepts OWF-CLA – to sign the agreement, click here.

Have your legal team review and sign the appropriate agreement.
Once the CLA is complete, use the OCP Specification Template and Design Package Guidelines to create your submission package.
If you need support, reach out to the OCP Project Community, including Project Leads or OCP Foundation Staff. They will assist you in presenting your contribution and collecting feedback.

Submit the document to the Project Leads in the respective Project Community and get approval from the Steering Committee. Ensure a supplier is available to build your product within 120 days (an OCP Solution Provider is preferred).

blocks.heading_html: Reference Architecture

blocks.body_html: Let's take a look at the steps for submitting a Reference Architecture contribution.

items_html: Start in the Contribution Portal.

Your reference architecture contribution must include:

  • At least two unique, tested configurations, or at least two unique OCP Accepted™ Product SKUs.

  • More than 50% content from orderable SKUs.

You must also provide product test documentation, certification information, and configuration details about the reference architecture and warrant that the reference architecture works as documented.

Submit the document to the Project Leads in the respective Project Community and get approval from the Steering Committee. If you are an OCP Solution Provider, OCP will publish your reference architecture on the OCP Contribution Database.

blocks.body_html:
There are several logos and certification marks we offer members who show expertise in designing, deploying, and optimizing scalable, energy-efficient data center infrastructures.

We award these specific attributes through our OCP Solution Provider Program.

This program enables members to position their products, solutions, facilities, and services to meet the growing OCP market opportunity.
Click the play icon to watch the video.
The OCP Solution Provider Program encompasses several sub-programs, including:

items_html: Having products recognized as OCP Accepted™.
Having a data center facility self certified as OCP Ready™.
Having a product approved as OCP S.A.F.E.™ and/or becoming an approved Security Review Provider (SRP).
Becoming a host for an OCP Experience Center.
Participating in the OCP Marketplace.

blocks.body_html: Let's take a look at how products, facilities, and services qualify to receive these logos and certifications.

blocks.body_html:
The OCP Product Recognition Program acknowledges products that align with an OCP approved contribution, allowing our members to promote their products and association with the OCP. It also helps potential adopters identify approved products and suppliers which are aligned with OCP's approved contributions.

Recognized OCP products are OCP Accepted™. This recognition comes with its own logo issued by the OCP Foundation.

Click the card to learn more.

back.description_html:
1. Available to all OCP Members.

  2. Must be a member of the OCP Solution Provider Program.

  3. A product can be recognized as OCP Accepted™ if it complies with an approved OCP specification AND design files have been contributed using the Design Package Guidelines.

blocks.body_html: To have a product recognized as OCP Accepted™, members must first submit the relevant collateral to the OCP Foundation team for review. This includes a product datasheet and/or a link to the product, along with an indication of the OCP-approved specification or contribution the product aligns with, as indicated in the OCP Contributions Database.

• Members must also include the relevant design files, following the Design Package Guidelines. 

  • The Foundation team then works with the relevant volunteer project leads to share this information, review, and mutually determine if the requirements have been met.

Once approved, members sign the relevant OCP Solution Provider and OCP Accepted™ Certification Mark Agreements and provide marketing collateral for the OCP Marketplace. The Foundation team will then provide ongoing quarterly OCP Marketplace Analytics as well as joint business development opportunities with the member.

blocks.heading_html: OCP S.A.F.E.™ Program

media.alt: OCP SAFE logo horz cmyk TM (1).png
media.source_asset: OCP SAFE logo horz cmyk TM (1).png

blocks.body_html: The OCP S.A.F.E.™ Program is engineered to streamline security audits, providing a centralized framework to ensure conformance and reliability for device consumers. By reducing redundancy and overhead in security assessments, the program aims to foster greater confidence in the security posture of hardware and firmware components across the supply chain.

There are two groups of members involved in S.A.F.E.

Click each card to learn more.

front.description_html: OCP Security Review Providers

back.description_html:
Third party security firms who perform security assessments on device firmware.

They are approved by the OCP Security S.A.F.E.™ Project Leads based on a set of requirements.
Members who have products with firmware they wish to have approved as OCP S.A.F.E.™

blocks.body_html:
Device manufacturers and approved OCP Security Review Providers work together under the S.A.F.E. framework to produce short form security audits which are available alongside OCP S.A.F.E.™ approved devices on the OCP Marketplace.

Let's take a look at the process of achieving OCP S.A.F.E.™ recognition.

items_html: Members choose from a list of approved OCP Security Review Providers to conduct a security conformance review.
The device will be designated an OCP S.A.F.E.™ approved product and listed on the OCP Marketplace once the OCP SRP submits the security conformance report.

The OCP Foundation team will issue the appropriate OCP S.A.F.E.™ logos to use with the device and provides ongoing quarterly OCP Marketplace Analytics as well as joint business development opportunities with the member.

blocks.complete_hint: Complete the content above before moving on.

blocks.heading_html: OCP Data Center Facilities Recognition

blocks.body_html: Colocation data center operators participating in the OCP Ready™ Data Center Recognition Program perform a detailed OCP Ready™ self assessment of their facilities to ensure they meet the rigorous standards and requirements set forth by the Data Center Facilities Project. Data Centers that self certify that they meet the OCP Ready™ requirements will receive an OCP Ready™ certification mark.
Click each step to learn how data centers are recognized as OCP Ready™.

items.description_html:
Members choose the data center site assessment that aligns with their data center design/specification and target market.

There are currently two versions of the site assessment:

  1. OCP Ready™ v2 for Hyperscale: For data centers catering to hyperscale operators, emphasizing site security, logistics, base building infrastructure, and MWs of power and cooling capacity for large-scale wholesale deployments.

  2. OCP Ready™ v1: For colocation data centers meeting OCP and industry best practices for high-density power, cooling, and physical infrastructure, optimized for OCP recognized hardware (e.g., Open Rack V2).

There is a site assessment required for each recognition:

  1. OCP Ready™ v2 for Hyperscale Data Center Site Assessment (Google Sheet) (Excel)

  2. OCP Ready™ v1 Data Center Site Assessment (Google Sheet) (Excel)
Potential members complete the assessment and contact the OCP Ready™ Program Lead to review their submission and discuss next steps.
Once the OCP Ready™ Program Lead confirms the potential member's assessment meets the requirements, they sign the required OCP Membership and Solution Provider agreements.

The member presents their completed data center site assessment to the Data Center Facility Community for final evaluation and approval.

The Data Center Facilities Project Leads, OCP Ready™ Program Lead (s) and members of the Foundation team are all involved in the approval of a data center.
Upon approval, the member executes the OCP Ready™ Certification Mark License Agreement and prepares promotional materials to be listed on the OCP Marketplace.
The member's data center is published on the OCP Marketplace, making it visible to a global audience.
The OCP Foundation team issues the OCP Ready™ Certificate and provides ongoing quarterly OCP Marketplace Analytics and joint business development opportunities with the member.

blocks.body_html:
OCP Solution Providers are eligible to host an OCP Experience Center. The primary focus of an OCP Experience Center is to accelerate open innovation and facilitate the widespread adoption of OCP-recognized equipment. Serving as a cornerstone in OCP's strategy to penetrate emerging markets, OCP Experience Centers complement the OCP Ready™, Product Recognition, and OCP S.A.F.E.™ programs.

The target audience for these centers includes adopters and channel partners seeking firsthand experience with OCP hardware. OCP Experience Centers can provide in-person or virtual access designed to provide proof points around OCP solutions, gaining a deep understanding of the benefits offered by OCP recognized equipment.

OCP Solution Providers reach out to the Foundation team to discuss the potential options for becoming a host and the Foundation team determines the viability of the center.

While project leads are not involved in this process, they are welcome to recommend potential members, technology areas or locations to establish an OCP Experience Center.

You can view all current OCP Ready™ Data Centers and OCP Experience Centers using the map below.

embed.description: OCP Ready™ certified data center facilities provide colocation services capable of supporting higher density compute, artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) workloads. OCP Experience Centers seed emerging markets by allowing potential adopters to see and understand OCP equipment, channel and system integrators to conduct presales and engineers to develop new pre-product concepts.

blocks.body_html: The OCP Marketplace is where vendors from across the OCP Community converge to offer a diverse variety of hardware products, solutions, facilities and services that adhere to the core tenets of OCP. The multi-vendor nature of the OCP Marketplace ensures access to a wide range of options, allowing potential adopters to tailor their infrastructure to meet their specific needs and preferences.

The OCP Marketplace consists of several sections, including: OCP Recognized Products, Chiplets, Integrated Solutions, OCP Ready™ Data Center Facilities, OCP Experience Centers, Telecom & Edge Solutions, as well as a dedicated section for AI.

All listings on the OCP Marketplace are from approved OCP Solutions Providers and is a great place to see where contributions meet the market in the form of products, solutions, facilities, and services.

Before we finish, let's recap what we've covered in this course.

items.title: Specifications
items.description_html:
Specifications are designed with a layered framework:

  • Base Specification: Provides a high-level framework for interoperable hardware and software.
  • Design Specification: Refines customer requirements.
  • Product Specification: Defines manufacturing requirements.

items.title: Recognition
items.description_html:
Products can receive OCP Accepted™ recognition when they comply with an approved OCP specification and their open-source design files are publicly available.

Data centers can be recognized as OCP Ready™ if they meet the OCP Ready™ requirements.

items.title: Tools
items.description_html:
We use Google Workspace and Zoom as our primary tools for communication, collaboration, and project tracking.

Please contact Michael Schill or Kevin Kifer for training and setup on all tools.

items.title: Types of Contributions
items.description_html:
OCP accepts 12 types of contribution:

  • Specifications
  • Design Files
  • Embedded Software
  • Products
  • Facilities
  • Reference Architectures
  • Tested Configurations
  • Case Studies
  • White Papers
  • Requirements Documents
  • OCP-Centric Content
  • Client Testimonials

items.title: Voting
items.description_html:
Any member of the OCP Community who belongs to an OCP Corporate Member organization can vote for Project Leads and Sub-Project Leads.

Only members from Silver, Gold, or Platinum Corporate Member organizations can vote for Steering Committee Representatives.

items.title: Leadership Roles
items.description_html:
There are four volunteer leadership roles at OCP, each with different requirements and responsibilities:

  • Steering Committee Representative
  • Project Lead
  • Sub-Project Lead
  • Workstream Lead

items.title: Types of Projects
items.description_html:
OCP consists of 12 key projects:

  • Cooling Environments
  • Data Center Facility
  • Hardware Management
  • Networking
  • Open Platform Firmware
  • Rack & Power
  • Security
  • Server
  • Storage
  • Sustainability
  • AI Computing Continuum
  • Time Appliances
